object_description: angular sports center formed by two buildings beneath a connected roof
design_condition: The two buildings are set laterally to preserve the spacious outdoor landscape and frame the pool area, but the large roof and extensive footprint intrude into the park and conflict with its free-flowing topography.

positive.statement: The lateral setting brings back a significant increase in space and the original spaciousness of the outdoor area.
The central hall creates a clear and easily found entrance gate to the facility.
The architecture respects the necessary distance from the outdoor pool, allowing the landscape to flow around it.
The operational arrangement of the ice rink promises good use.
The indoor pool is organized on one floor with a pleasant reference to the outdoor pool.
The noise insulation of the open ice rink works well.
The ideas for the wider area provide beneficial additions to the sports and leisure facility.
The supporting concept is simple and requires moderate spans.

negative.statement: The transition zones between different uses are insufficiently controlled and precise.
The massive roof does not provide enough atmospheric support for the outdoor pool's identity.
The large footprint causes relatively high sealing and prevents green roofs.
The paths and terrain adjustments do not yet fit well into the existing park.
Scattered seating elements contradict the character of the park pool and appear interchangeable.
The separate entrances weaken the clarity of the shared reception arrangement.
The upper floor is not easily accessible for disabled people.
The indoor pool's expansive canopy may prevent daylight and eye contact with the outside.
The project has high creation costs because of its large roof, facade areas, volume, and excavation.
The iconic silhouette failed to convince the jury at this location.
